text: This service reads every fact it does not own through a published contract: case, party, queue and task facts from rwb-case, and the business date and load time of each data product from rwb-source-data. It reads no recovery.v_ace_* view, holds no copy of an ACE column and opens no connection to the ACE tables.
why: Architecture v5 (higher in precedence) makes the views readable by rwb-source-data alone and gives the S9 row two REST cells, to P5 and to Outside, with no cell to P1 or to the ACE database.
read: The FSD constraint and its five freshness validation rules as a statement of which facts the steps need, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 1; Section 6 FR-S9-041, FR-S9-042; Section 8.2; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S9-01
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 owner, before wave 1 system test
impact: If a view stays readable by this service, the boundary test and the freshness guarantee would each need a second owner.

text: This service calculates the fee from the contracted schedule in force and the recorded result, holds the claim and its approval, and records the matched recovery it is given. The money is matched and paid by rwb-payment, and the match result reaches this service through a contract; this service calls no ALS, no general ledger and no payment interface on any path.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives payment, proceeds matching and fees to rwb-payment and gives this service the items panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees and scorecards; the slide 13 matrix gives the S9 row no cell to P8.
read: FSD A2.7 and A2.9 as the fee behaviour the business needs, with the payment execution read as P8's capability.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 5 CAP-S9-007, CAP-S9-009; Section 6 FR-S9-024, FR-S9-025, FR-S9-031; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S9-02
confirm: Solution architect with the P8 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: Two writers of one payment would leave the fee claim and the posting unable to agree.

text: This service owns the six items Architecture v5 names (panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees, scorecards) in schema rwb_partner. Three physical tables keep their names and fields as the Ownership Map, the Logical Data Model and the physical schema give them (partner, partner_user, partner_instruction); the scorecard, the fee claim, the review, the conduct sample and the field visit are named here as entity groups, and their physical names are written with the DB story.
why: Architecture v5 slides 17 and 41 give the six items and the Ownership Map and the physical schema hold three tables.
read: The three published tables as the substance and the remaining three items as entity groups.
confirm: Data architect, before the S9 DB story
impact: The migration and the boundary test cannot be written for the three entity groups until their tables are named; the stories are not blocked.

text: partner_instruction.case_id is held as a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key out of schema rwb_partner, and the link to the case is enforced at the rwb-case contract.
why: ADR-014 and DP-01 forbid a foreign key across schemas, and Architecture v5 slide 29 gives each service its own schema and login with no cross-schema access.
read: The Logical Data Model type CROSS_REF uuid and the relationship N:1 to recovery_case as the meaning of the link, not as a physical constraint.
confirm: Data architect with the platform DB owner, before the S9 DB story
impact: A cross-schema key would make the per-service restore and the per-service login impossible to demonstrate.

text: The eight catalog columns are read as the partner and instruction entity: six partner columns and partner_instruction.case_id and partner_id. The fields of the scorecard, the fee claim, the review, the conduct sample and the field visit are not stated in this document and are written with the story that first needs them.
why: The FSD repeats the same eight columns in ten features and carries no field catalog in the other five, so no source lists the remaining fields.
read: The repeated catalog as the one field list the FSD actually gives.
confirm: Business analyst, S9 with the data architect, before wave 4 story writing
impact: A field added silently would escape the classification and masking review.

text: The allocation rule, the score, the fee approval, the review, the conduct sample, the extra-cost approval and the field capture are authored from FSD A2.3, A2.4 and A2.8 to A2.15, governed in rwb-decision and evaluated in this service with the embedded Drools kit; the chase, the recall, the exit, the conflict, the insolvency, the conduct breach and the re-selection use R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29 and R-UNI-45 as they stand.
why: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 has no partner route set, while the Temporal and Drools Design gives this module the universal rules for the recall path and names its own decisions on slide 25.
read: The universal rules as the recall and exit engine, and the FSD features as the source of the decisions that have no rule row.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 7; Section 6 (Rule column); Section 10.5; Section 12 OQ-S9-06
confirm: Center of excellence analyst with the P7 owner, before wave 4 release
impact: A decision taken without a governed rule row is a decision the log cannot reproduce from its version.

text: The monthly scorecard and the conduct sample run as Temporal Schedules in rwb-partner through the workflow kit, created with the story that first needs them, and each carries a run book, monitoring and an alert.
why: The job map holds no S9 job while both features need a monthly trigger, and DP-10 replaces Quartz with a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service.
read: FSD A2.8 and A2.13 step 1 ('Receives its trigger') as a schedule that the owning service holds.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 6; Section 6 FR-S9-026; Section 9; Section 10.5; Section 12 OQ-S9-07
confirm: Solution architect with the platform workflow owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: Without a schedule the scorecard is built when someone remembers, which is the practice the product replaces.

text: Each FSD acceptance criterion is read as the main success statement of its feature, the two exception criteria of each feature are carried as they stand, and the product-level criteria in section 11 of this document are authored here from the rules and the feature text.
why: All fifteen main success rows are the same sentence with the story note 'Written one epic ahead', and no feature has an alternate flow or a background event.
read: The generic criteria as placeholders for the step behaviour described in A2.x.2 and A2.x.3.
confirm: Business analyst, S9 with the Product Owner, before wave 4 story writing
impact: A criterion written from a placeholder cannot fail, so a story could be accepted without the behaviour.

text: The two EP01 slices RWB-S9-E1032-APP and RWB-S9-E1057-APP keep wave 1 as a contract-only slice: the partner identity and the partner document path are published and faked, and no panel, allocation or fee behaviour is promised in wave 1.
why: Rule R5.6 keeps the wave map wave for a story whose wave is earlier than its service's wave, and the two stories are document-intake paths that belong to the document hub in wave 1.
read: The split plan slice as a contract obligation on this service rather than as a build in this service.
confirm: Solution architect with the programme manager, before wave 1 system test
impact: If the slice is read as a build, the service must be created two waves early and the wave-4 plan is void.

text: The two EP02 slices RWB-S9-E2019-APP and RWB-S9-E2034-APP keep wave 2 as the partner identity and portal contract slice: the partner_user binding, the FAPI 2.0 route and the portal contract are published and faked, and the panel screens are delivered in wave 4.
why: Rule R5.6 keeps the wave map wave, the partner portal is first needed by the PRT-01 screen in E2, and the Ownership Map ruling gives partner_user to S9.
read: The split plan slice as the identity and portal contract this service owes wave 2.
confirm: Solution architect with the programme manager, before wave 2 system test
impact: Partners without a published identity binding cannot sign in for the E4 and E5 instructions.

text: InstructionWorkflow on queue rwb-partner, the event InstructionIssued (EV-20) and the event PartnerResultSubmitted (EV-21) are published as a contract ahead of wave 4, so rwb-litigation (wave 3) and rwb-asset (wave 3) build against the contract and its fake and the instruction works when this service lands.
why: Architecture v5 gives the S4 and S5 rows a Temporal call and an event subscription to S9, while the program creates S9 in wave 4 after both releases.
read: BRD Q-019 and section 7.3 as an ordering problem to be solved by contract-first delivery rather than by moving the service.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S9-016, CAP-S9-017; Section 9; Section 10.2; Section 12 OQ-S9-10
confirm: Solution architect with the S4 and S5 owners, before wave 3 system test
impact: Without the early contract, two wave-3 releases carry an instruction that has no owner until April 2027.

text: The monthly scorecard, the review outcome and the conduct result reach the partner review forum and the steering measures through rwb-reporting, built from the events and the decision record; this service ships no Power BI extract.
why: Architecture v5 removes the data lake and DP-17 removes the data lake interfaces, while the FSD still names Power BI in A2.8.
read: A2.8's Power BI line as the reporting need, not as an interface this service builds.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 6 FR-S9-027; Section 9; Section 10.5; Section 12 OQ-S9-11
confirm: Solution architect with the P9 owner, before wave 4 release
impact: A second reporting channel would duplicate a measure the log already produces.

text: The extra partner cost on a held asset is recorded and approved in this service against the asset reference the asset module publishes, and AMIS is reached through one agreed path with rwb-integration rather than by a direct call from this service.
why: The slide 13 matrix gives the S9 row no cell to S5, P1 or P2, while FSD A2.14 names AMIS and requires FEAT-AST-07.
read: A2.14's integration points as the facts the approval needs, with the calls owned elsewhere.
confirm: Solution architect with the S5 and P2 owners, before wave 4 system test
impact: A direct AMIS call from this service would add an unmanaged interface to the DMZ.

text: The four partner screens PRT-01 to PRT-04 are served through the partner gateway, and the three staff screens SCR-34, SCR-35 and SCR-36 through a gateway-bff composite route; the owner of each screen is recorded with the story that first needs it.
why: Architecture v5 gives the partner screens to the partner gateway and the staff screens to gateway-bff, and no register names a screen owner.
read: The FSD first-in column as the wave each screen is needed in, not as the wave this service is created in.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S9-039; Section 9; Section 10.5; Section 12 OQ-S9-13
confirm: Solution architect with the platform edge owner, before wave 2 system test
impact: An unowned screen is a screen no story builds and no release demonstrates.

text: The staff paths keep the v5 REST base /api/recovery/partner/v1 behind gateway-bff and the portal paths keep /partner/v1/* behind the partner gateway; both are published in one service contract.
why: Architecture v5 slide 17 gives two REST entries and DP-13 gives one base, and the Ownership Map lists endpoints on both.
read: R4 and DP-13 as the naming rule for staff paths, with the portal base as the external channel the partner gateway fronts.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S9-039, FR-S9-043; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S9-14
confirm: Solution architect with the platform edge owner, before the S9 contract story closes
impact: Two bases with no recorded rule leave the gateway route and the screen client undefined.

text: The capability area of this module is PARTNER_PORTAL as LOV-CAPABILITY holds it, and partner_instruction.instruction_type and status use LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS.
why: The FSD names the capability area without naming it and gives two lists only, while the Logical Data Model holds all three.
read: The FSD exception criteria as a permission check against a capability area, with the area taken from the list the model publishes.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S9-004; Section 8.1; Section 8.4 rule 1; Section 12 OQ-S9-15
confirm: Security administrator with the business analyst, S9, before wave 4 release
impact: A permission check against an unnamed area cannot be tested across roles.

text: One owner role per partner type is held as a versioned panel row read at run time, and an allocation is refused where the type has no owner role.
why: REQ-S9-002 is Must for E6 and no feature or field carries it, while principle 1 makes every value a business person may change a versioned data row.
read: REQ-S9-002 as a data requirement on the panel rather than as a screen.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S9-002; Section 6 FR-S9-003; Section 8.1; Section 8.4 rule 1; Section 12 OQ-S9-16
confirm: Partner and agency manager with the business analyst, S9, before wave 4 release
impact: A partner type with no owner is work nobody is accountable for, which is the condition the requirement removes.

text: rwb-access keeps the internal role model and the delegation table, the partner gateway enforces the external identity with FAPI 2.0 and multi-factor authentication, and this service holds the partner_user binding that scopes a partner user to one firm and one partner role.
why: The program trace delivers REQ-ACA-012 with rwb-access, and the Ownership Map ruling and the Logical Data Model give partner_user to S9.
read: REQ-ACA-012 as a control split between the edge, the access service and this service.
applied_in: Section 3; Section 6 FR-S9-038; Section 8.1; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S9-17
confirm: Security administrator with the P4 and S9 owners, before wave 2 system test
impact: Two stores of one partner identity would let a partner user act for a firm it does not work for.

text: The three partner tables carry the Workbench record class, and the periods stay open until DL26 answers; the partner, its instructions and its results stay readable after an exit.
why: NFR-028 and NFR-031 leave every period open under DL26 and the FSD states no class for this module.
read: A2.12 as a state change on the partner record, not as a deletion.
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 4 release
impact: An exit that deleted the record would erase the instructions and the fees of an ended contract.

text: rwb-writeoff decides the post charge-off treatment and posts the recovery after charge-off, and rwb-partner issues and tracks the placement instruction on that decision and holds the panel, the terms, the recall and the fee.
why: BR-059 sources the placement from S7's requirements while FEAT-PRM-06 is an S9 feature, and R-WO-30 to R-WO-35 carry the transitions.
read: The two requirement rows as one behaviour split at the instruction.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 5 CAP-S9-006; Section 6 FR-S9-019, FR-S9-020, FR-S9-021; Section 12 OQ-S9-19
confirm: Solution architect with the S7 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: Two writers of one placement would leave the case placed twice or not at all.

text: The four reused messages keep their published wording, and the module's own refusals, holds, differences and breach notices are authored with the story from the Error and Message Standard in Thai and English.
why: The FSD uses MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 only, and NFR-059 requires both languages under DL10.
read: The reused messages as the shared standard, with the module-specific wording still to be written.
confirm: Business analyst, S9 with Legal counsel and Compliance, before wave 4 release
impact: A message written in one language only fails NFR-059 at the first screen review.

text: The scorecard measures, their weights, the thresholds and the panel capacity rule are versioned data rows, and the initial set is agreed with the scorecard story; this document states no value.
why: Every FSD feature repeats one metric with a 100 percent target and no source states a measure, a weight or a threshold.
read: The repeated metric as an example measure, not as the scorecard definition.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S9-028; Section 8.4 rule 1; Section 12 OQ-S9-21
confirm: Partner and agency manager with the center of excellence analyst, before wave 4 release
impact: A scorecard with invented weights would allocate real work on an invented rule.

text: The BRD is read as approved for this run: the Business Requirements Program v5 and Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 are treated as the approved baseline for BR-059, BR-060, BR-070 and BR-071, and no approval is recorded in this document. The version status is Draft and the approval table of section 13 is empty.
why: The run rule removes human approval stops, and the BRD governance table records no Product Owner decision for this module that could be read from the sources.
read: The requirement text, the priorities and the epic column as the approved baseline; the approval itself as an open item.
confirm: Product Owner and FDA, before the PRD is baselined
impact: A Draft PRD drives story writing; the approval is what makes the baseline binding.

text: Version 1 is the next version of this family. No PRD for S9 existed in the PRD folder, so this document is a first version and no earlier PRD content is carried.
why: The folder 03 PRD directory held no S9 file before this run.
read: The absence of the file as a first version, not as a replacement.
confirm: Document owner, at the review of this version
impact: None on the content; the version number is the first of the family.

text: FSD S9 Partner management versions 1 and 2 are earlier versions of the baseline v3. Their dates and change notes are not in the sources read, so they are carried as an open item rather than reconstructed.
why: The v3 change note refers to v2 and the document control gives version 3 only.
read: The missing history as an open item.
confirm: Document owner, at the review of this version
impact: None on the requirements; the change history is incomplete.

text: The CAP, FR, NFR, AC, journey, role and open-question identifiers of this document are new and exist only here; the FSD requirement, feature, rule, message, list, screen and acceptance criterion identifiers are carried unchanged.
why: The realignment needs product-level identifiers that the FSD does not hold, and the FSD identifiers must stay stable for traceability.
read: The generated identifiers as this document's own, with the source identifiers in their own columns.
confirm: Document owner, at the review of this version
impact: None; the two identifier families are kept apart on purpose.

text: The BR to CAP to FR/NFR to AC rows are carried inside this document at section 11.2 and are not appended to the traceability matrix in this run, because the matrix is a master file the assembler stage owns.
why: The write-only list of this work package does not include the matrix file, and the master files are written only by the assembler.
read: The matrix append as an assembler task fed by section 11.2.
confirm: Assembler stage owner
impact: Until the assembler runs, the end-to-end trace lives in this document only.

text: The fee claim is approved through the approval workflow on rwb-decision by Temporal call, with the delegation limit read at run time as the other route services do it, and the local decision record is sealed in the central ledger through rwb.decision-record.v1.
why: The matrix gives the S9 row no P7 cell while every other route service shows T to P7 for its DoA approvals, and slide 15 gives the approval workflow and the limits to rwb-decision.
read: The matrix note on DecisionRecorded as the record path, and the approval route as the same Temporal path the other services use.
confirm: Solution architect with the P7 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: A fee approved without the route leaves money leaving the bank on a screen decision.

text: The monthly scorecard, the review outcome, the conduct result and the override rate reach the partner review forum from the decision record and from two additional events on rwb.partner.events.v1, and rwb-reporting subscribes to them; this service ships no separate report extract.
why: REQ-S9-007 requires the report, ADR-018 makes reporting a read model from events, and no S9 to P9 edge exists today.
read: REQ-S9-007 as a reporting obligation satisfied through the event platform.
confirm: Solution architect with the P9 owner, before wave 4 release
impact: A forum report assembled by hand is the practice REQ-S9-007 removes.

text: The contractual notice on a missed target is issued through rwb-comms by Temporal, from its approved template, and this service subscribes to the proof-of-delivery event; the notice decision, the template version, the approver and the cure period stay in this service.
why: The FSD requires the notice, Architecture v5 gives the notice content and the proof of delivery to rwb-comms, and the slide 13 S9 row gives this service no cell to P6.
read: A2.11 as the notice behaviour the business needs, with the notice content and the delivery read as P6's capability on the same terms rwb-litigation uses.
applied_in: Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S9-033; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S9-23
confirm: Solution architect with the P6 owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: A notice with no proof of delivery cannot start a cure period the bank can defend.
